searchLog.query: Japanese L2 vowel length and consonant length perception Tsukada Tajima
searchLog.outcome: Read vowel study abstract, Tajima training paper, Tsukada 2020 full paper and its rendered Table 1. Exact table-derived provenance restricted to eight matching words.

searchLog.query: Japanese fricative gemination and devoicing perception
searchLog.outcome: Read Sadakata 2014 full-text sections and Yamakawa 2022 abstract. Did not import pseudo words or claim these studies validate the authored real-word bank.

searchLog.query: TUFS Japanese long vowels, t/d, k/g, consonant-glide modules
searchLog.outcome: Read university teaching explanations; kept educational motivation separate from study evidence.

searchLog.query: Official EDRDG JMdict basic Japanese–English dictionary download and licence
searchLog.outcome: Downloaded official JMdict_b.gz via www.edrdg.org, edition 2026-10-01; parsed exact spelling/reading entries and inspected relevant senses. FTP-host certificate did not validate; primary www host succeeded. No bulk dictionary included. Glosses adapted with CC BY-SA attribution.
Bare-word paths generally failed; one indexed 黄色 entry confirmed the selected きいろ reading. No broad Kotobank verification claimed.

sources.title: Okada (1991): Japanese — Illustrations of the IPA
sources.locator: JIPA 21(2), pp.94–96; vowel-length examples and conventions on p.95.
sources.whatItSupports: Tokyo-area sound inventory, length contrasts, predictable consonant variants, high-vowel devoicing and independent pitch accent.
sources.limitations: Descriptive illustration of one speaker, not learner-training evidence. Our IPA conventions normalize its older symbols and omit pitch labels. No recordings reused.

sources.title: Vance (2001): Japanese — Orthography and Basic Phonology
sources.locator: NINJAL-hosted two-page excerpt; consonant and vowel tables, moraic segments and accent.
sources.whatItSupports: All five vowels have quantity contrasts; moraic nasal realization is context dependent; ordinary Japanese distinguishes the selected consonant categories.
sources.limitations: Short descriptive sketch, not a study of the chosen words. Broad /ɴ/ below is a moraic-nasal placeholder, not a claim of invariant uvular articulation.

sources.title: Tokyo University of Foreign Studies: Long Vowels
sources.locator: Explanation, Long Vowels 2.2.1.
sources.whatItSupports: Pedagogical distinction between one- and two-mora vowels; usual long-vowel readings of kana ei/ou and the need to separate orthography from sound.
sources.limitations: General teaching description, not word-specific phonetic validation. Selected /eː,oː/ readings require later recording review; no blanket conversion of every ei/ou sequence.

sources.title: Tokyo University of Foreign Studies: k / g
sources.locator: Explanation, k / g 1.6.1.
sources.whatItSupports: Japanese /k–ɡ/ is an instructional priority for learners whose native laryngeal categories differ.
sources.limitations: Pedagogical motivation, not a controlled efficacy experiment; no ranking of all learner populations implied.

sources.title: Tokyo University of Foreign Studies: t / d
sources.locator: Explanation, t / d 1.5.1.
sources.whatItSupports: Japanese /t–d/ can be misidentified through different native-language laryngeal cues.
sources.limitations: Teaching guidance, not proof that these word pools or this training method are effective.

sources.title: Tokyo University of Foreign Studies: Consonant-glide
sources.locator: Explanation, Consonant-glide 1.11.1.
sources.whatItSupports: A contracted consonant-glide mora must not be expanded into an additional full /i/ syllable.
sources.limitations: Supports the moraic interpretation of contracted sounds; not an experiment on the particular /s–ɕ/ pool.

sources.title: Tsukada, Hirata & Roengpitya (2014): Cross-language perception of Japanese vowel length contrasts
sources.locator: PubMed abstract; JSLHR 57(3), 805–814; DOI 10.1044/2014_JSLHR-S-12-0416.
sources.whatItSupports: American English, Italian and Thai listeners were tested on Japanese vowel length with AXB discrimination.
sources.limitations: Abstract inspected; full stimulus list not recovered. Evidence concerns the length class, not every vowel-specific bank or training success. No word receives stimulus provenance from it.

sources.title: Tajima et al. (2008): Training English listeners to perceive phonemic length contrasts in Japanese
sources.locator: Full paper, JASA 123, 397–413; abstract and pp.398–400 on temporal context and training.
sources.whatItSupports: Vowel-length identification training and tests of rate, word position, presentation context and transfer. Results support treating those variables explicitly.
sources.limitations: Reported generalization was limited. Identification with feedback is not our cross-word audio-only ABX; the paper does not establish its superiority. No word-list membership imported here.

sources.title: Tsukada, Kim & Han (2020): Perception of Japanese consonant length by native speakers of Korean differing in Japanese learning experience
sources.locator: Interspeech 2020, pp.4471–4475; methods §2 and Table 1 on p.4472.
sources.whatItSupports: Korean learner groups completed /t,k/ length AXB trials with three different speakers per trial.
sources.limitations: Cross-sectional perception, not randomized training. X differed in speaker/token, not necessarily lexical word; this is not a validation of our cross-word design.

sources.title: Tsukada, Kim & Han (2020): Table 1, Japanese word stimuli
sources.locator: Table 1, p.4472, directly read in text and rendered PDF image.
sources.whatItSupports: Documents the exact selected readings/senses saka, kako, haka, sakka, kakko, oto, wata and otto. Three retained paired frames also share the table’s accent-type grouping.
sources.limitations: Only those eight matching lexical items receive this source in stimulusSourceIds. Hakka meaning mint is not our 発火 ignition. Remaining words are editorial dictionary additions; no audio permission inferred.

sources.title: Sadakata et al. (2014): Language specific listening of Japanese geminate consonants
sources.locator: Abstract and introduction; materials use pseudo words containing /ss/ and manipulated silence-plus-/s/.
sources.whatItSupports: Cross-language perception provides context for sustained-frication geminates.
sources.limitations: Does not directly test our real-word /s–sː/ comparison or training method. Pseudo words were not imported.
sources.license: Article CC BY; no recordings reused.

sources.title: Yamakawa, Amano & Kondo (2022): Perceptual boundary and discrimination sensitivity of Japanese singleton and geminate stops
sources.locator: Publisher abstract; Acoustical Science and Technology 43(2), 96–104.
sources.whatItSupports: Adjacent vowel devoicing and speaking rate affected stop-length perception in Japanese and Taiwanese Mandarin listeners.
sources.limitations: Abstract inspected; not certification of our lexical exemplars. No stimulus membership assigned.

Pitch accent is an independent lexical dimension and is not a target here. No Tokyo accent dictionary was imported; exact accent patterns remain to be reviewed before audio/trial balancing.
